title.narrative: Women driving resilience in agriculture and rural areas, UN WOMEN
Women driving resilience in agriculture and rural areas, UN WOMEN

description.narrative: Project aims at removing structural barriers, by introducing time and labor-saving technologies, innovating sources of financing, enabling women to be better prepared to cope with challenges, to improve their livelihoods and socio-economic situation of their families in rural areas.

Projektet syftar till att undanröja strukturella hinder, genom att introducera tids- och arbetsbesparande teknik, innovativa finansieringskällor, vilket gör det möjligt för kvinnor att vara bättre förberedda på att klara utmaningar, att förbättra deras försörjning och socioekonomiska situation för sina familjer på landsbygden.

The overall objective of the contribution aims at removing structural barriers, by introducing time and labour-saving technologies, innovative sources of financing, enabling women in BIH to be better prepared to cope with the challenges, including change-related risks, improving their livelihoods and socio-economic position and the lives of their families.
The proposal includes two outcomes: 1) mainstreaming gender consideration into policy making, institutional budgeting, planning, programming and monitoring processes to create an environment conducive for women farmers, women-led agri-businesses, cooperatives, associations and networks. 2) establishing integrated approach to address problem pf women from rural areas limited access to economic opportunities. This will be done in the view of strengthening resilience to climate change risks both from the supply and demand. More specifically, outcomes are expected to be achieved through implementation of the three complementary Outputs.
When it comes to measurable quantitative impact, the project's goal is to capacitate the total of at least 200 women who will benefit from safeguarded or new jobs and improved livelihoods. Addressing both supply and demand side, the project will on the supply side mobilize private sector agriculture finance to improve the access to commercial funding sources for at least 50 women. On the demand side at least 180 women farmers/entrepreneurs will receive training modules on identifying agricultural practices to enhance environmentally sound and sustainable agricultural production. It is also expected that over 50 government officials and policy makers relevant for identifying and addressing gender inequalities in agriculture and rural development sector will be trained.
Moreover, the project is also expected to strengthen the country's entrepreneurship climate and overall agribusiness industry with a particular focus on engagement of women and their integration into structured agricultural value chains. Another significant market development which this project is expected to generate concerns the evolution of agricultural finance in BiH, especially the financial products and services accessible by women borrowers.

During the reporting period the project in terms of Outcome 1: "Enhanced enabling environment for women-led agri-entrepreneurship through the removal of structural barriers, including the development of social and gender responsive agricultural and local rural development policies." the project team has conducted series of activities in line with the Project Document. When it comes to expected results the project drafted the gender mainstreaming and mapping of vulnerabilities to climate change in agriculture and rural development, that was later validated by both entities in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The report consists of two fold assessments: a) gender mainstreaming in agriculture and rural development b) a mapping of the vulnerabilities of rural women and men with regards to climate change and it identifies a gender gap. It is important to note that this report is largely based on comprehensive gender assessment produced by UNW and FAO in 2021. The project reports that there were series of workshops and validations exercises were conducted aiming to finalize the reports and receive required validations.
In terms of Outcome 2 "Improved Economic position of women in agriculture and rural areas, as a result of improved access to business management and sustainable/climate-smart agriculture, assets, tools and technologies" similarly the project measured expected results - a series of activities resulting in initiation of Needs Assessment of Public and Private Financial Institutions that Provide Support for Women Farmers aimed at identify barriers and potential solutions to enhancing financial opportunities for women in rural areas. The project also conducted comprehensive research related to women´s access to finances in rural areas materializing in draft study report titled "Access to finances for women in agribusiness and rural areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina. " The study serves as an in-depth analysis of of financial mechanisms, challenges and opportunities for women engaged in agriculture in particular in reference to climate finance. It is anticipated that the report will be completed during the next reporting period. the project also organized a workshop for 25 representatives including private banking sector to gain knowledge on "Gender sensitive lending solutions for economic activities in rural areas". Further assessment of different sources of financing for women agri-business and rural tourism owners, farmers, associations and cooperatives on national and entity level including financing provided by international financial institutions and donor organizations was completed. The assessment represents a useful document in understanding existing regulatory framework and mapped financing sources targeting women from rural areas, agricultural entrepreneurs etc.
Within the same outcome the project team developed the gender - sensitive criteria that will be applied. The criteria includes various aspects such as legal status, economic and sector - specific needs, local conditions and provides for comprehensive and inclusive approach to support women in rural areas. Trainings were organized for women in agri-business and wider to improve digital and literacy skills to access relevant sources of financing, including increasing their financial capacities, application abilities, business planning, marketing.
Lastly, the project also completed a report on Gender Responsive Assessment of Value Chains in the Selected Rural Areas in BIH and 32 participants were trained on gender sensitive selection of the priority value chains. Two gender Assessment in Sustainable Production and Management in Pilot Rural Regions were completed focusing on farmers´ needs, skills and assets. On the basis of these pilots training plan was developed, covering the area of marketing, application of digital technologies etc. 32 women improved their knowledge about practical use of digital tools and information supporting their farming and non-farming activities.
In reviewing the indicators it is clear that project mainly focused on development of studies and needs assessments accompanied with organization of workshops that are considered as trainings which are all expected results. However, there are number of substantive activities that have not yet been initiated while the project is entering its final year of implementation. The project team in the report states that in the final year the focus will be placed on fund distribution in partnership with entity ministries and that work with Farmer Field Schools. The delay in implementation is considered as unexpected result particularly in terms of grant distribution component.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
